title: Pomelo Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Pomelo Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Pomelo nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and magnesium in suha, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Pomelo nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your suha (pomelo) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, zinc, phosphorus and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which pomelo nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a pomelo nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest pomelo nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in pomelo

Pomelo leaves show it as other citrus do. Older leaves turn pale green, then yellow, evenly with no clear pattern, and drop early, so the canopy thins. New leaves are small, thin and light green, flushes are short, and the tree flowers sparsely and sets a light crop. You see it most at this stage: flowering and after harvest. At both stages, nitrogen is among the nutrients that hold pomelo back the most.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in suha
Trees fed little or irregularly, sandy or leached soils, heavy rain, waterlogging. Raw straw or manure that ties nitrogen up as it rots.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also yellows older leaves but leaves a green V at the leaf base and is worst next to the fruit. Sulfur deficiency starts on young leaves. To be sure, leaf test: pick leaves three and four on branches that are 3 months old. Use 4 to 6 month old leaves from twigs without fruit. Get a soil analysis to set the rates.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply nitrogen in the weeded ring, split into two equal doses: when the rains begin, to build vigour before flowering. Again as the rainy months draw to a close. Plan on urea, complete fertilizer, muriate of potash and chicken dung each year, with the amounts set by the soil test. For quick greening, give a Urea spray at 2 percent (20 grams per liter, 320 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days for citrus. Give about 100 grams of Urea 46 0 0 a tree for each year of age, up to 1 to 2 kg for a bearing tree, split between the first rains and the last, under the canopy edge.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.

To keep it away, fertilize every year by the soil test, ring weed before each dose and mulch. Go easy on ammonium fertilizers. Years of heavy ammonium nitrogen can drop soil pH from about 5.7 to 4.3 and bring on magnesium shortage.
Potassium deficiency in pomelo

Leaf signs follow citrus: the edges of older leaves turn pale yellow or bronze, then the yellow spreads, and new leaves are small. In pomelo the cost shows most in the crop. Well fed with potash, bearing Magallanes trees flower far more, set and hold many more fruit, and give heavier fruit with thinner peel and more juice. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and the first two months of fruit growth. Flowering and fruit set peak in April, and flushing peaks in June.
Why potassium deficiency happens in suha
Sandy or leached soils, heavy rain, soils rich in magnesium, and nitrogen fed without enough potash. But each heavy crop carries potash away.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on older leaves, but leaves a green V at the base. Salt or fertilizer burn scorches edges on leaves of all ages. To be sure, leaf test of the third and fourth leaves from 3 month old branches, and a soil test for potash, magnesium and calcium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

The usual basal dose is 150 grams of potassium (K) per tree, about 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60. 225 grams of potassium per tree (about 450 grams of Muriate of potash) gave much more flowering, fruit set and yield. Adding a foliar potash spray to the basal dose helped further. Time the doses before flowering and in the two months after fruit set. For quick help, spray Potassium nitrate 13 0 46 or Sulfate of potash at 1 percent (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer).

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.

To keep it away, give potash every year along with nitrogen, and more on trees carrying heavy crops. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Magnesium deficiency in pomelo

Older and middle leaves yellow between the veins. As in other citrus, the yellow starts near the leaf base on each side of the midrib and spreads until only the tip and a V shaped area at the base stay green, then the leaf turns yellow to bronze and drops. Limbs carrying heavy fruit show it most. Where the soil is short of magnesium, up to a third of the leaves in an orchard can show this yellowing. You see it most at this stage: fruit growth, on heavily bearing limbs.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in suha
Acid soils, especially soils acidified by years of heavy ammonium fertilizer, high rainfall that leaches magnesium, and heavy potash. Seedy fruit draw more magnesium than seedless kinds.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole tree evenly. Potassium deficiency bronzes the leaf edges. To be sure, leaf test and a soil test for pH, magnesium, potash and calcium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

On acid soils use Dolomite. Aim for pH 5.5 to 6.5 and lime below pH 5. Where the soil test shows low magnesium, give magnesium at 20 percent of the nitrogen rate, as Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite. Spray Magnesium sulfate at 4 percent (40 grams per liter, 640 grams in a 16 liter sprayer), about 7 liters per tree over three monthly sprays. With much less NPK, this lifts leaf magnesium and eases the yellowing. A 4 percent spray is strong, so try it on a few branches first.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime with dolomite, avoid overusing ammonium fertilizers, and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Zinc deficiency in pomelo

The signs match those on other citrus. Young leaves show yellow patches between the veins with an uneven green band along the midrib and main veins (mottle leaf). In severe cases new leaves are small, narrow, pointed and upright, twigs die back. Fruit on weak twigs stay small with low juice. You see it most at this stage: new flushes.
Why zinc deficiency happens in suha
High pH and limed soils, heavy phosphate, heavy poultry manure, organic soils and cold wet spells.
How to tell it apart

Citrus greening (HLB) is the main look alike and, with tristeza, one of the main causes of low citrus production in the country. Do the pen test: zinc deficiency looks the same on both sides of the midrib, HLB blotches do not. To be sure, pen test, then a zinc spray on a few branches and a look at the next flush. If the mottle stays uneven, send leaves for an HLB laboratory test. A leaf test helps.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray zinc on each new flush when leaves are two thirds to almost fully expanded. Spray Zinc sulfate at 0.5 to 1 percent (5 to 10 grams per liter, 80 to 160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with half as much hydrated lime, every two weeks on the new flush. Zinc on the soil does not work on limey soils. Give 50 to 100 grams of Zinc sulfate a young tree and 100 to 250 grams a bearing tree a year under the canopy.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc), **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur) and **Nemes Foliar** by SCL Filipinas (4.8 0 0 with 10 percent zinc, 4.9 percent boron and 4.8 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the pH below 6.5, avoid heavy phosphate, include zinc in regular sprays, and control psyllids. Test the soil every two or three years.
Phosphorus deficiency in pomelo

Leaf signs are weak and follow citrus: older leaves lose their deep green, partly yellow. May show a dull bronze or purplish cast with small freckles along the main veins. Flowering and fruit set are poor, leaves and fruit drop early, and fruit are coarse, with a hollow core and sour juice. Phosphorus is often the nutrient that holds pomelo back most at flowering, fruit growth and after harvest. You see it most at this stage: all through the cycle. Most felt at flowering and fruit set.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in suha
Strongly acid soils where iron and aluminium lock phosphorus up, limey soils, low organic matter, cold wet soil and weak roots.
How to tell it apart

A thick peel does not prove phosphorus shortage, because Magallanes trees given more potash grow a thinner peel. So low potash can thicken it too. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test of the third and fourth leaves from 3 month old branches.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer by the soil test. Complete fertilizer belongs in the pummelo budget every year. Superphosphate suits soils of any pH, but do not use DAP 18 46 0 on alkaline soils. Lime soils below pH 5 so phosphorus stays available. Give 200 to 500 grams of Complete 14 14 14 a young tree, up to 1 to 2 kg a bearing tree, when the rains begin.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole, keep the pH at 5.5 to 6.5, and add compost or chicken dung.
Boron deficiency in pomelo

Pomelo shows boron shortage as other citrus do. Fruit stay small, hard and misshapen, with gum pockets and dark spots in the white inner peel and sometimes in the core, and many drop. The growing tip dies and the shoot branches out. Young leaves curl and their veins split and turn corky. You see it most at this stage: flowering to fruit growth, often after a long dry spell.
Why boron deficiency happens in suha
Sandy and alkaline soils low in organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium, drought, and fertilizers with no micronutrients.
How to tell it apart

Too much boron is a real risk in pomelo. Giving 100 grams of borax per tree a year, split in two doses, can poison the tree. To be sure, soil and leaf test for boron before adding any. Soil boron below 0.5 mg per kg is short, and above 5 mg per kg is toxic.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Give a Borax spray at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter, 80 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) for citrus. Use boron on the soil or as a spray, never both. Keep soil doses small and only on soils that test low. Give 25 to 50 grams of Borax a young tree and 50 to 100 grams a bearing tree a year, spread evenly under the canopy.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use fertilizers that carry micronutrients, keep organic matter up and water during dry spells. Never repeat big borax doses without a test. Test the soil every two or three years.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any pomelo nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your suha needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Pomelo nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my suha leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole tree pale green to yellow, old leaves falling early, thin canopy and few flowers. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: Apply nitrogen in the weeded ring, split into two equal doses: when the rains begin, to build vigour before flowering. Again as the rainy months draw to a close.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: The usual basal dose is 150 grams of potassium (K) per tree, about 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60. 225 grams of potassium per tree (about 450 grams of Muriate of potash) gave much more flowering, fruit set and yield.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: On acid soils use Dolomite. Aim for pH 5.5 to 6.5 and lime below pH 5.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my suha lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the pomelo nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
